newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul Exchange to list leading polyester firm.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul Exchange to list leading polyester firm.

text.p: Seven percent of the share capital of Turkey's leading polyester fibre and thread producer SASA Suni ve Sentetik Elyaf Sanayii A.S. will begin trading on the Istanbul Stock Exchange's national market on Friday, the Exchange said.
The opening price will be 7,200 lira per 1,000 lira nominal valued share.

SASA, owned by Sabanci group, one of Turkey's leading industrial conglomerates, is to list 360.5 billion lira, or seven percent of its 5.15 trillion lira share capital via a two-day public offer last week.
A 15-member consortium led by T. Sinai Kalkinma Bank and co-led by T. Is Bankasi managed the offer.

T.Sinai Kalkinma said 181 billion lira of the offer was sold to 35,042 domestic individual investors, 25 billion lira to 34 domestic institutional investors and 154.5 billion to 16 foreign institutional investors.

It said Citibank Asset Management which bought 36.2 billion lira worth SASA shares, Pictet Asset Management 19.68 billion lira and Battery March 25.33 billion lira of shares were the leading foreign buyers.
SASA, the biggest industrial unit in the Sabanci group, will be the 11th group firm with shares listed on the Exchange.

Sabanci Holding's stake in SASA stands at 24.9 percent. The group's banking arm and Turkey's biggest private commercial Akbank's stake in SASA fell to 36.8 percent after the public offer from previous 43.8.
SASA has a yearly polymerisation capacity of 246,000 tonnes and DMT (raw material) production capacity of 123,000 tonnes which it plans to raise to 246,000 tonnes in 1998.
The bulk of its output is used in the textile sector and the rest in the packaging sector.
